title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: S over T, E a sheaf of O_S-modules with a stratification relative to T, written as its 'Taylor map' δ = δ^∞_E : E → P^∞_{S/T}(E) (principal parts of infinite order). P is an E-torsor (an affine torsor). The previous page showed that a stratification on P compatible with δ is the same as a morphism of sheaves λ: P → P^∞_{S/T}(E)/δE satisfying two conditions. (27) says λ(x+ξ) = λ(x) + p(d^∞_{S/T}ξ), where d^∞ is the universal Taylor map for the other structure and p is the projection. (28) says λ lands in the horizontal sections (P^∞(E)/δE)^♮.

Section 3 of the page compares stratifications with integrable connections on affine torsors. A stratification of P compatible with δ trivially induces a connection on P compatible with the connection d^0_E of E. The task is to write the corresponding map d^0_P : P → E⊗Ω^1_{S/T} explicitly in terms of description (17)/(26).

Tool: let P^∞(E)^+ = ker(ε: P^∞(E) → E), the sections vanishing on the diagonal, i.e. I_Δ·P^∞(E). Since ε∘δ = id_E, δ splits ε. Hence the composite P^∞(E)^+ ↪ P^∞(E) → P^∞(E)/δE is an additive isomorphism (29). Its inverse, composed with the projection p, is φ ↦ φ − δ(ε(φ)) (29'). The isomorphism is only additive because δ and the inclusion are linear for different O_S-structures.

Through (29), λ becomes λ^+: P → P^∞(E)^+ (30). Condition (27) becomes (31): λ^+(x+ξ) = λ^+(x) + d^+(ξ), where d^+(ξ) := d^∞(ξ) − δ^∞_E(ξ). This uses ε(d^∞ξ) = ξ.

The next page reduces modulo I_Δ^2, using P^1(E)^+ = E⊗Ω^1. There d^+ becomes the connection ∇_E (the difference of the two first-order Taylor maps), and λ^+ becomes d_P with d_P(x+ξ) = d_P(x) + ∇_E ξ. This is the affine connection on P. Its class in H^1_DR(S,E) is the image of the stratified class under the canonical map (24), which is an isomorphism in characteristic 0 with Ω^1 flat.

Left-margin note: define the 'integrable' sections of P^∞(E)^+ as those corresponding to the horizontal sections of P^∞(E)/δE. Caution: the inclusion P^∞(E)^+ ↪ P^∞(E) is not compatible with the stratifications, so horizontality cannot simply be read off inside P^∞(E).

Purpose: a torsor-theoretic comparison of stratified (crystalline-type) H^1 with de Rham H^1 of a stratified module. This serves the construction of Gauss–Manin connections via nonabelian or affine H^1.
errors: No mathematical error. (29) is correct because δ is a section of ε, and the inverse φ ↦ φ − δε(φ) is right. The rewriting of (27) as (31) is correct because ε∘d^∞ = id.

Gap that Grothendieck flags himself: the additive isomorphism (29) is not compatible with stratifications or module structures. Condition (28) therefore has to be transported to define 'integrable' sections of P^∞(E)^+, which is done only in the margin as a to-do.

Notation drifts across pages: d^0_P here versus d^*_P / d^b_E on the next page. The verification that the reduction gives the connection and the H^1 class is marked 'faire la vérification' and is not carried out.

ideas.what: Stratification on an E-torsor compatible with a stratification on E induces an (integrable) affine connection on the torsor
ideas.modern_name: Torsors under a crystal / affine torsors with integrable connection; H^1 of the crystalline or stratifying site versus de Rham H^1
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck, 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (1968); Berthelot (1974); Mazur–Messing (1974) for torsors and extensions with connection
ideas.where_published: Closely related material in 'Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes' (Dix exposés, 1968), but not this explicit torsor formalism

ideas.what: Splitting P^∞(E) = δE ⊕ P^∞(E)^+ using the augmentation, giving the additive isomorphism P^∞(E)^+ ≅ P^∞(E)/δE via φ ↦ φ − δε(φ)
ideas.modern_name: Decomposition of jets along the augmentation ideal; difference of the two Taylor maps giving the connection
ideas.where_published: EGA IV 16 (principal parts); Crystals and de Rham cohomology

ideas.what: d^+ = d^∞ − δ^∞ as the infinite-order 'connection' of a stratified module, reducing mod I^2 to ∇
ideas.modern_name: Infinite-order Taylor-map formulation of stratification (HPD-stratification difference operator)
ideas.where_published: Implicit in the Crystals exposé and Berthelot's thesis

deep.surprise_reason: This is a careful but routine formalization of how stratified affine torsors give integrable connections and of the comparison map on H^1. The material is standard in crystalline theory (Grothendieck 1968, Berthelot, Mazur–Messing). Nothing here appears new to specialists.
transcription_corrections: Line 3: the inserted phrase is 'compatible à δ)' and the crossed word is 'toute'; the connection is 'compatible à d^0_E'.
Margin: the target should read '(P^∞_{S/T}(E)/δE)^♮' (horizontal sections, as on the previous page), not '^♭'.
In (29') the crossed-out symbol before φ looks like 'd^+_E' (struck); the formula is φ ↦ φ − δε(φ), where ε is the augmentation.
Margin last lines: 'P^∞_{S/T}(E)^+ ↪ P^∞_{S/T}(E) n'est pas compatible avec stratifications'; the next page's 'd^*_P' / 'd^b_E' should consistently be d^0_P / d^0_E.
